subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup move from pairing by default to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom, while preserving explicit pairing-mode configs?
rationale: The code change is straightforward but the decision changes first-run trust, owner identity capture, and upgrade/default semantics for a security-sensitive channel.

options.title: Token-verified allowlist default
options.body: Fresh setup generates a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, writes allowlist config, and keeps explicit pairing configs intact.

options.title: Defer to broader default policy work
options.body: Keep this issue open but resolve it only as part of the cross-channel post-bootstrap default decision in the related broader issue.

options.title: Post-bootstrap auto-flip only
options.body: First-run pairing remains unchanged, but a later owner-derived allowlist default is handled by the broader post-bootstrap policy work.

recommendation.title: Token-verified allowlist default
recommendation.body: Fresh setup generates a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, writes allowlist config, and keeps explicit pairing configs intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to the Telegram docs/runtime and shared channel ingress/default surfaces involved in the decision.
